what: known-clean control, and a MINIMAL PAIR with wrong-01 — identical base, identical leg C (which adds the verbatim near-duplicate appendix). The single difference is that here leg A edits the ROLLBACK paragraph instead of the anchored one. The anchored block therefore survives into the merge unchanged, the mechanism sees two exact matches, disambiguates on prefix/suffix context, and picks the right one. The harness must stay silent.
why_this_matters: A near-duplicate ALONE is not a silent-wrong merge: context disambiguation handles it. The defect needs BOTH legs to act — one editing the anchored block out of the exact-match set, one resurrecting its old bytes. That is why a single-leg rebase cannot reach it.
